state.product: MenteViva, iOS cognitive-exercise app for older adults. Warm, no-fail, big-target design, EN+ES, offline, zero third-party dependencies, solo developer on a free Apple account (no cloud sync, no TestFlight). Copy ceiling: 'fun mental exercise', no medical claims. Daily picks and difficulty are decided on the device by rules: easy/medium/hard per game, step down below 65% accuracy, step up at 90%+ over 3+ sessions, at most one step per 7 days.
state.player: Primary player: the owner's father, early-stage dementia, plays alone on his own iPad. Caregiver and buyer: the adult child, who visits and receives a weekly share text.
state.games: Memory Lane (emoji pair matching, 6/8/10 pairs), Name the Herd (pick the items of a category), Quick Eyes (an item flashes, find it among 4), Color Clash (Stroop), Number Trail (arithmetic streaks). Points were removed from the UI after players found them confusing; sessions store accuracy, rounds and duration.
state.playtest_findings: Structured family playtest: Memory Lane, Name the Herd and Quick Eyes held his attention; Color Clash and Number Trail fell flat. The one major concern: Memory Lane looks childish ('it is a game, but he is not a child'): cartoon emoji, and at 8-10 pairs the cards are too small and need scrolling. Some finished sessions do not appear in the weekly history (a save bug, being fixed). The owner wants results and, above all, progression tracked across weeks. Family photos already exist on his iPad.
state.owner_decisions: The player sees progression as warm words plus an icon, never numbers and never a down arrow. The caregiver sees real numbers in an open Family section in Settings and in a richer weekly share text. The caregiver can set each game's difficulty (Auto by default, or pin Easy/Medium/Hard) and hide games per device; Color Clash and Number Trail will be hidden from his library with the code kept. Auto-difficulty keeps weekly steps.
state.candidate_games: reminiscence_photos: look at one of his own photos with gentle prompts, no wrong answer. sayings_completion: finish a familiar saying or proverb from 3 big choices (EN/ES). everyday_sequencing: put 3-4 picture steps of a familiar routine in order (making coffee). spot_the_difference: two near-identical calm scenes, tap the change, hints after a pause.

build_order.instructions: After the save bug is fixed, which workstream should be built first?

criteria.progress_tracking: Weekly progression: warm per-game line for the player, real numbers and trend for the caregiver, richer share text
criteria.family_settings: Family section: per-game difficulty (Auto or pinned) and hide/show games per device
criteria.memory_lane_adult_refresh: Make Memory Lane look adult: no scrolling, larger cards, calmer styling
criteria.photo_content: Bring his own family photos into the app

familiar_content_first.instructions: What is the best first way to bring his own family photos into the app?

criteria.photo_memory_lane: His photos become Memory Lane card faces: reuses the game he already plays, directly fixes the childish look, smallest build
criteria.reminiscence_game: A separate errorless photo-reminiscence game: one photo at a time with gentle prompts, no matching
criteria.both_photo_lane_first: Photo card faces in Memory Lane now, the separate reminiscence game next

memory_lane_adult_fix.instructions: When no family photos are chosen, how should Memory Lane stop looking childish?

criteria.adult_restyle_emoji: Keep emoji but restyle for adults: at most 8 pairs on a grid that fits the screen with no scrolling, larger cards, calm refined palette, a real card back
criteria.bundled_real_images: Ship a bundled set of real photographs of everyday objects (needs licensed or self-made images)
criteria.line_icons: Replace emoji with Apple's built-in monochrome line icons on large cards

progress_signal.instructions: Which single signal best represents a game's progression week over week for this player, driving both the warm player line and the caregiver trend?

criteria.accuracy_trend: Mean accuracy this week versus the previous week
criteria.difficulty_level: The difficulty level the rules have reached for the game
criteria.speed_trend: Median time to finish a session

show_decline_to_caregiver.instructions: Should the caregiver view show a game's downward trend explicitly (for example 'accuracy lower than last week')?

criteria.true: The caregiver needs honest data to adjust difficulty and notice change; the player never sees it
criteria.false: Week-to-week dips are noise for one player and invite a medical reading the app must not make

add_games_now.instructions: Should new games be added now, rather than first deepening the 3 games that worked (save fix, progress, Memory Lane look, photos)?

criteria.true: Three visible games are too thin; the earlier boredom finding needs variety soon
criteria.false: Fix saving, progress and Memory Lane first; each new game multiplies polish and translation work

quick_eyes_keep.instructions: Quick Eyes held his attention in the playtest. Should it ship as is, deferring the planned untimed redesign?

criteria.true: Observed engagement beats the matrix prediction; redesign only if frustration appears
criteria.false: The timed flash still conflicts with errorless design for early dementia; redesign anyway
